objective: Proof. In a knot's space the 2-edge cuts arrange the units in cycles: an open arc of m units acts as x + y = m (mod 2) on its two channels (routes compose into parity contacts, hub-free), and closing an odd cycle is the failure. Native separation: an intervention at two junctions of a cycle meets every route between two arcs; before it they are related, after it they are independent. Across 3-edge cuts, tight cuts of splice trees are laminar and give a canonical tree of routes through hubs; in cyclic spaces tight cuts cross and no tree is canonical. No route carries a magnitude: parity routes remember one bit (the parity of their length), hub routes equality; so the knot's spaces give native paths and separation but no native extended distance.
status: Proved by NATIVE-PATHS-20261101-001B-P001: routes between the parts of a knot's space are fixed by the space (every nontrivial 3-edge cut is a proper splice cut or the shift of a 2-edge cut, with a twist rule; in ten spaces the proper splice cuts never cross each other or a 2-edge cut; relabelling-invariant) and carry at most one bit (an arc of m units accepts x + y = m mod 2; between two units two routes of opposite parity, whose disagreement is the failure; a hub side is one point or one line whatever it contains); cutting junctions separates exactly when both routes are met (2998 cases); counts 5 per unit, 5^m per arc, a count of quantified witnesses; read against the program's definitions these are routes of a declared substrate, not native paths of complete contacts
title: Native routes and separation, and no length
